explanation: Exotic species are nonnative organisms that migrate or are introduced by humans into an ecosystem. Introduction pathways include colonization, horticulture/agriculture, and accidental transport. Islands are highly vulnerable to exotic species due to their geographic isolation and lack of native defenses. The notes provide two examples: 1) Japanese Kudzu vines: imported to the Southern U.S. to control soil erosion, they spread rapidly and overtook native plants. 2) Mongoose: introduced to Hawaii to control rat populations, they instead began preying on native birds.

questions.q: Why was the mongoose introduced in Hawaii, and what was the actual ecological result?
opts: To control salmon; they ended up preying on zooplankton.
To control rat populations; they ended up preying on native birds instead.
To stop soil erosion; they ended up preying on Kudzu vines.
To provide medicinal value; they ended up causing eutrophication.
questions.exp: The notes state: 'Mongoose introduced in Hawaii to control rat pop. Now prey on native birds.'

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of an exotic species introduced to control erosion that ended up smothering native vegetation in the Southern US?
questions.exp: The notes mention 'Japanese Kudzu vines brought in to Southern US to stop erosion; overtake native plants.'
